text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- A Portuguese hotel chain will be established in Mexico, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus told the paper during a visit to the country.
- Profits per share of retailer Jeronimo Martins rose 23 percent in the first nine months of 1996, compared to the same period in 1995.
- Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor (BPSM) posted 8.03 billion escudos consolidated net profit in the first nine months of 1996. The figure is not comparable with the previous period.
- Petrol prices could rise one to two escudos per litre next Thursday. The price of diesel should remain unchanged.

- Sonae Industria signed a joint venture with a subsidiary of Anglo-American Zimbabwe, Border Timber, to set up a wood products factory in Zimbabwe. Sonae and Border Timber will hold equal shares in the joint venture. The value of the joint venture is expected to be around five billion escudos.
- Retailer Jeronimo Martins said it was studying the possibility of launching a bid for mineral water company Vidago.
- An agreement for Saudi Aramco to take a stake in Portuguese oil company Petrogal could be announced in December, Saudi sources told the paper.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, during an official visit to Mexico, accused international financial institutions of applying principles too rigidly.
- German group Hoechst plans to expand textiles production in Portugal and to invest 800 million escudos in a new factory in Mem Martins near Lisbon.
